answer: To protect an agent nebula from Sybil attacks, protocols can anchor peer identities to slashable collateral bonds. Participants must lock scarce capital to vouch for new nodes, forcing an adversary to incur compounding liquidity costs per persona rather than floating a costless zephyr of fake identities. Misbehavior triggers automated slashing of staked collateral. However, this design inherently disadvantages low-capital honest agents and risks oligarchic centralization.
